claims.claim: Direct-to-storage upload via pre-signed URLs keeps 10MB bytes off app servers (CAP-02)
claims.evidence: Consistent across Architecture Overview, AD-01, and CAP-02 mapping; standard and correct pattern for S3-class storage.

claims.claim: Virus scan and thumbnail run async off a queue, gated by status before retrieval (CAP-03/CAP-04/CAP-05)
claims.evidence: AD-02 and AD-03 describe queue-driven worker + quarantine-until-clean gate; coherent with mapping table.

claims.claim: Librarian skill was unavailable this run
claims.evidence: Stated L7; cannot be independently confirmed from outputs, but consistent with no persistence occurring.

workarounds: Librarian unavailable — worked from inline breakdown and provided a retrieval query for an agent with librarian access.

suggestions.assertion: Object/blob storage is recommended for stored files
suggestions.reason: Trivially satisfied by any upload architecture; consider strengthening to require quarantine/clean separation or a status-gated retrieval, which is the discriminating safety property.

No assertion checks that retrieval is gated until a clean scan (the core security correctness of an upload+scan feature). All three runs implemented this well, but the eval wouldn't catch a design that serves files before scanning completes.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions comprehensively cover structure and process. Adding one correctness assertion on the scan-before-serve gate would make the suite more discriminating.
